nodes.author: CasualtySurgeon
nodes.text: @thatsnotmine125 @AmandaPritchard @NHSEngland Pre-Covid I looked after lots of patients on ICU who were intubated and ventilated for (presumed bacterial) pneumonia. When you washed their lungs out with water (bronchoalveolar lavage) and sent it off for PCR... you found RSV or metapneumovirus and not a whiff of bacterial DNA.

nodes.author: thatsnotmine125
nodes.text: @CasualtySurgeon @AmandaPritchard @NHSEngland Given you recognise these people were being ventilated, then you recognise they were having treatment. So the conclusion being people with viral illness may need treatments for their symptoms.

nodes.author: CasualtySurgeon
nodes.text: @thatsnotmine125 @AmandaPritchard @NHSEngland Twitter is not a good platform for this kind of discussion. We had moved on to discussing whether a doctor can distinguish a viral from bacterial chest infection. I have not disputed that patients with viral infections never need treatment.

nodes.author: thatsnotmine125
nodes.text: @CasualtySurgeon @AmandaPritchard @NHSEngland None of this changes the fact people who feel unwell should seek medical advice. It is not their job to know anything at all about viral illness, or its treatment.

nodes.author: CasualtySurgeon
nodes.text: @thatsnotmine125 @AmandaPritchard @NHSEngland I've no problem with people seeking healthcare advice if they feel they need it. I *do* have a problem with the Chief Executive of the NHS telling patients they'd better seek help early for viral infections because they are easier to treat then.

nodes.author: thatsnotmine125
nodes.text: @CasualtySurgeon @AmandaPritchard @NHSEngland I think you’re reading it in a strangely literal way. She’s not suggesting seeking antivirals. She’s saying if you have viral illness then seek advice if needed, then suggests people like the pharmacist.

nodes.author: CasualtySurgeon
nodes.text: @thatsnotmine125 @AmandaPritchard @NHSEngland If @AmandaPritchard thinks everyone who feels unwell should have contact with a healthcare professional and as soon as possible in their illness then the NHS is already sunk.

nodes.author: thatsnotmine125
nodes.text: @CasualtySurgeon @AmandaPritchard @NHSEngland I don’t think suggesting someone go to the pharmacy is particularly wild to be honest.
